acceptance: faillearn and ciwatch items are written by the filing writer (red: each writes its JSON itself)
A minted item that repeats a filed id is still an idempotent skip, not a failure
Two concurrent mints of one id file exactly one item (a race test with the lock)
Each minter's degraded path is unchanged when the writer refuses or faults
fix: Keep File's rules strict and move the minters: each mints the full shape (summary, fix, acceptance) and files through File, or through a library function File and the minters share that lives beside inboxbatch.Item, so the minters need no Mover. A lane-side minter must take the inbox `.bump.lock` (verifylock.AcquireAt, as inboxmover/root_failure.go does) around the id scan and the link, since several lanes can mint at once.

source: console, 2026-09-30, split from inbox-add-cli acceptance 3 and the architecture review of `evolve inbox add`
summary: `evolve inbox add` (lifecycle.(*Mover).File) is the operator's filing writer: it validates against the readers' schema, refuses a duplicate or retired id, an unknown dependency and a lifecycle-owned field, and never overwrites a file. The two kernel minters still write items directly and in other shapes: faillearn writes id/title/weight/kind/priority/files/injected_by (no summary, fix or acceptance), ciwatch writes no fix and no acceptance. Readers must keep tolerating those shapes until both converge. Acceptance 3 of inbox-add-cli, split out when the verb landed; the architecture review of the verb found the second minter and the race below.
title: The kernel minters (faillearn's retrospective floor, ciwatch) write inbox JSON themselves instead of through the filing writer (lane part)
